data.gender_notes: Rehmatun is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Arabic word 'rehmat', which means mercy or grace. This name is often given to a newborn girl as a sign of hope for a blessed and compassionate life. The name Rehmatun carries the meaning “Gift of Mercy” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Rehmatun usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of mercy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine gift of mercy and compassion, instilling a deep sense of empathy and kindness in the heart of the bearer.
data.etymology: Rehmatun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift of Mercy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rehmatun total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rehmatun" holds a deep cultural significance in the Islamic world. By naming a child Rehmatun, parents express their desire for blessings from Allah (God) and hope for a wonderful and compassionate life for their child. The name adds to the community's collective memory and strengthens the bond of kinship between families, as it signifies the importance of showing compassion and kindness to one another. The name is a reminder of the Islamic ideal of treating all human beings with mercy and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Rehmatun" lies in its resonance with the Islamic concept of mercy and compassion. As Muslims, it is our belief that mercy and compassion are essential qualities of Allah and that He is the "Most Merciful" (Ar-Rahman) and the "Most Compassionate" (Ar-Rahim) of all. By bestowing this name upon a child, parents are reminding themselves and their child of the need to embody the qualities of mercy and compassion in their daily lives. It is a reminder to be kind to others, to be patient and forgiving, and to extend help and assistance to those in need, just as Allah has shown mercy and compassion to us.
